question: Given the function $f(x)=\frac{a^{x}+a^{-x}}{2},(a>2)$ then $f(x+y)+f(x-y)$ is equal to

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Given, $f(x)=\frac{a^{x}+a^{-x}}{2}$ Then, $f(x+y)+f(x-y)=\frac{a^{x+y}+a^{-(x+y)}}{2} +\frac{a^{x-y}+a^{-(x-y)}}{2}$ $=\frac{a^{x}\cdot a^{y}+a^{-x}\cdot a^{-y}+a^{x}\cdot a^{-y}+a^{-x} a^{y}}{2}$ $=\frac{a^{x}(a^{y}+a^{-y})+a^{-x}(a^{y}+a^{-y})}{2}$ $=\frac{(a^{x}+a^{-x})(a^{y}+a^{-y})}{2}$ $=2\cdot\frac{a^{x}+a^{-x}}{2}\cdot\frac{a^{y}+a^{-y}}{2}=2 f(x) f(y)$ © examsnet.com

question: Let $a, b$ be non zero real numbers such that $a b = \frac{5}{2}$ and given $A=\begin{bmatrix} a & -b \\ b & a \end{bmatrix}$ and $AA^{T}=$ $20I$ (I is a unit matrix), then the equation whose roots are a and b is

question: If $(x^{2}+5x+5)^{x+5}=1$ then the number of integers satisfying this equation is

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $\because (x^2+5x+5)^{x+5}=1$ For an integer power to equal $1$ , the possibilities are: the exponent is $0$ with a nonzero base, the base is $1$ , or the base is $-1$ with an even exponent. Case I $x+5=0$ $\Rightarrow \; x=-5$ Here the base is $5 \ne 0$ , so $x=-5$ is valid. Case II $x^2+5x+5=1$ $\Rightarrow \; x^2+5x+4=0$ $\Rightarrow \; (x+1)(x+4)=0$ $\Rightarrow \; x=-1,-4$ Both are valid. Case III $x^2+5x+5=-1$ and $x+5$ is even. $\Rightarrow \; x^2+5x+6=0$ $\Rightarrow \; (x+2)(x+3)=0$ $\Rightarrow \; x=-2,-3$ For $x=-2$ , the exponent is $3$ , which is odd, so it is not valid. For $x=-3$ , the exponent is $2$ , which is even, so $x=-3$ is valid. Thus the integer solutions are $x=-5,-4,-3,-1$ . Hence the number of integers satisfying the equation is $4$ . © examsnet.com
transcription_status: published educational transcription; original PDF remains authoritative

question: Let $f(x)=x^{3}+a x^{2}+b x+c$ be polynomial with integer  coefficients. If the roots of $f(x)$ are integer and are in  Arithmetic Progression, then  a  cannot take the value _______

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $f(x)=x^{3}+a x^{2}+b x+c$ Let roots of $f(x)$ are $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ and since roots are in AP. $\therefore \; \; 2\beta = \alpha + \gamma$ Now, Sum of roots $\alpha + \beta + \gamma = -a$ or $2\beta + \beta = -a$ or $\beta = -\; \frac{a}{3}$ It is given that, roots are integers. $\therefore \beta$ is an integer when $a$ is multiple of 3 . Option (a), (c) and (d) are multiple of 3 . $\Rightarrow \; \; a \neq 1214$ © examsnet.com

question: The sum of the roots of the equation $e^{4 t}-10 e^{3 t}+29 e^{2 t}-22 e^{t}+4=0$ is _______

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $e^{4 t}-10 e^{3 t}+29 e^{2 t}-22 e^{t}+4=0$ ...(i) Let $e^{t}=x$ and roots of (1) be $t_{1}, t_{2}, t_{3}, t_{4}$ $\therefore x^{4}-10 x^{3}+29 x^{2}-22 x+4=0$ Then, roots are $x_{1}, x_{2}, x_{3}, x_{4}$ product of roots $x_{1} \cdot x_{2} \cdot x_{3} \cdot x_{4}=4$ $\Rightarrow e^{t_1}\cdot e^{t_2}\cdot e^{t_3} e^{t_4}=4$ $\Rightarrow e^{t_{1}+t_{2}+t_{3}+t_{4}}=4$ $t_{1}+t_{2}+t_{3}+t_{4}=\log_{e}\;4=\log_{e}\;2^{2}=2\log_{e}\;2$ Sum of roots $=2\log_{e}\;2$ © examsnet.com

question: If a person has 3 coins of different denominations, the number of different sums can be formed is

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: 3 different coins of denominations Rupee 1, 2,5 and 10. Formula used: ${}^n C_r = \frac{n!}{r! \times (n-r)!}$ Calculation: There are 3 combinations to have the different sum of money Any 1 coin at a time $= {}^3 C_1$ $\Rightarrow \frac{3!}{1! \times (3-1)!} = 3$ Any 2 coins at a time $= {}^3 C_2$ $\Rightarrow \frac{3!}{2! \times (3-2)!} = 3$ All 3 coins at a time $= {}^3 C_3$ $\Rightarrow \frac{3!}{3! \times (3-3)!} = 1$ Sum of all combination $\Rightarrow 3+3+1=7$ $\therefore$ Total 7 different sums of money can be form. © examsnet.com

question: There are 7 identical white balls and 3 identical black balls.  The number of distinguishable arrangements in a row of all  the balls, so that no two black balls are adjacent is _______

solution: Solution: Number of white balls $=7$ Number of black balls $=3$ $\times W \times W \times W \times W \times W \times W \times W \times$ $\times$ are the places in row where black balls can be placed, which are  8 in number for 3 black balls. answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

question: $\tan 2\alpha \cdot \tan(30^{\circ}-\alpha)+\tan 2\alpha \cdot \tan(60^{\circ}-\alpha)$ $+\tan(60^{\circ}-\alpha) \cdot \tan(30^{\circ}-\alpha)$ is equal to

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

question: If $\tan^{-1}\left[\frac{1}{1+1.2}\right]+\tan^{-1}\left[\frac{1}{1+2.3}\right]+\cdots$ $+\tan^{-1}\left[\frac{1}{1+n(n+1)}\right]=\tan^{-1}[x]$ , then $x=$

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{1+1 .2}\right)+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{1+2 .3}\right)+\dots +\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{1+n(n+1)}\right)=\tan^{-1}(x)$ $\Rightarrow \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2-1}{1+1 .2}\right)+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3-2}{1+2 .3}\right)+\dots +\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{n+1-n}{1+n(n+1)}\right)=\tan^{-1}(x)$ $\Rightarrow \tan^{-1}(2)-\tan^{-1}(1)+\tan^{-1}(3)-\tan^{-1}(2)+\dots +\tan^{-1}(n+1)-\tan^{-1}(n)=\tan^{-1}(x)$ $\Rightarrow \tan^{-1}(n+1)-\tan^{-1}(1)=\tan^{-1}(x)$ $\Rightarrow \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{n+1-1}{1+(n+1) .1}\right)=\tan^{-1}(x)$ $\Rightarrow \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{n}{n+2}\right)=\tan^{-1}(x)$ $\Rightarrow x=\frac{n}{n+2}$ © examsnet.com

subject: Mathematics
question: In a △ABC, if $a=3, b=4$ and $\sin A=\frac{3}{4}$ then $\angle CBA=?$

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: △ABC, $a=3, b=4$ and, $A=\frac{3}{4}$ $\therefore \cos A = \sqrt{1-\sin^{2} A} = \sqrt{1-\frac{9}{16}} = \frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}$ But $\cos A = \frac{b^{2}+c^{2}-a^{2}}{2 b c}$ $\Rightarrow \frac{\sqrt{7}}{4} = \frac{4^{2}+c^{2}-3^{2}}{2 \cdot 4 \cdot c}$ $\Rightarrow 2 \sqrt{7} c = 7 + c^{2}$ $\Rightarrow c^{2} - 2 \sqrt{7} c + 7 = 0$ $\Rightarrow (c - \sqrt{7})^{2} = 0$ $\therefore c = \sqrt{7}$ Now, $\cos B = \frac{c^{2}+a^{2}-b^{2}}{2 a c}$ $\Rightarrow \cos B = \frac{7+9-16}{2 \cdot 3 \cdot \sqrt{7}} = 0$ $\Rightarrow B = 90^{\circ}$ $\therefore \angle CBA = 90^{\circ}$ © examsnet.com

question: In $\Delta ABC, A=75^{\circ}, B=45^{\circ}$ then the value of $b+c\sqrt{2}=$

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $A=75^{\circ}, B=45^{\circ}$ , then $C=180^{\circ}-(75^{\circ}+45^{\circ})=60^{\circ}$ $\because \frac{a}{\sin A}=\frac{b}{\sin B}=\frac{C}{\sin C}=2R$ where R is circum  radius $\Rightarrow a=2R\sin A, b=2R\sin B, c=2R\sin C$ Then, $b+c\sqrt{2}=2R(\sin B+\sqrt{2}\sin C)$ $=2R(\sin 45^{\circ}+\sqrt{2}\sin 60^{\circ})$ $=2R\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}\right)=2R\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$ $=2\cdot 2R\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2\sqrt{2}}\right)$ $=2\cdot\left(2R\sin 75^{\circ}\right)$ $=2\left(2R\sin A\right)$ $=2a$ © examsnet.com

question: If the volume of the parallelopiped formed by the vectors $\hat{i} + a \hat{j} + \hat{k}, \hat{j} + a \hat{k}$ and $a \hat{i} + \hat{k}$ becomes minimum, then $a=$

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Let $p = \hat{i} + a \hat{j} + \hat{k}$ $q = \hat{j} + a \hat{k}$ $\Rightarrow r = a \hat{i} + \hat{k}$ Volume of parallelopiped $= [pqr]$ $= p \cdot (q \times r)$ $V = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & a & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & a \\ a & 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$ $\Rightarrow V = a^{3} - a + 1$ Differentiating V with respect to a $\frac{dV}{da} = 3 a^{2} - 1$ Again, differentiating w.r.t. a $\frac{d^{2} V}{d a^{2}} = 6 a$ For stationary points $\frac{dV}{da} = 0$ $\Rightarrow 3 a^{2} - 1 = 0$ or $a^{2} = \frac{1}{3} \text{ or } a = \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ At, $a = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ $\frac{d^{2} V}{d a^{2}} = 6 \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} > 0$ ∴ Volume is minimum at $a = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ © examsnet.com

question: Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}, \vec{b}=\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}=7\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+11\hat{k}$ then the area of parallelogram having diagonals $\hat{a}+\hat{b}$ and $\hat{b}+\hat{c}$ is

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $a=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ $b=\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$ $c=7\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+11\hat{k}$ Then, $a+b=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+6\hat{k}$ and $b+c=8\hat{i}+12\hat{j}+16\hat{k}$ $=4(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})$ Area of parallelogram $=\frac{1}{2}\left|(a+b)\times(b+c)\right|$ $=\frac{1}{2}\left|2(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})\times4(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})\right|$ $=\frac{8}{2}\left|(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})\times(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})\right|$ $=4\left|\begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 \end{vmatrix}\right|=4\left|\hat{i}+\hat{2j}-\hat{k}\right|$ $=4\sqrt{1+4+1}=4\sqrt{6}$ sq units © examsnet.com

question: If $a$ and $b$ are two vectors such that $\left|a\right|=2,\left|b\right|=3$ and $a+t b$ and $a-t b$ are perpendicular, where t is a positive scalar, then

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $\left|a\right|=2,\left|b\right|=3$ $\because (a+t b) \perp (a-t b)$ $\Rightarrow (a+t b) \cdot (a-t b)=0$ $\Rightarrow a \cdot a - t(a \cdot b) + t(b \cdot a) - t^{2}(b \cdot b)=0$ $\Rightarrow \left|a\right|^{2} - t^{2} \left|b\right|^{2}=0$ $\Rightarrow t^{2} = \frac{\left|a\right|^{2}}{\left|b\right|^{2}}$ $\Rightarrow t = \frac{\left|a\right|}{\left|b\right|} = \frac{2}{3}$ © examsnet.com

question: If the axes are rotated through an angle $45^{\circ}$ , the coordinates of the point $(2\sqrt{2},-3\sqrt{2})$ in the new system are _____

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Let m be the slope of one of the lines given by $a x^{2}+2 h x y+b y^{2}=0$ Then, the other line has slope $m^{2}$ . $\therefore m+m'=\frac{-2 h}{b}$ and $m \cdot m^{2}=\frac{a}{b}$ $\because (m+m^{2})^{3}=m^{3}+(m^{2})^{3}+3 m \cdot m^{2}(m+m^{2})$ $\left(-\frac{2 h}{b}\right)^{3}=\frac{a}{b}+\frac{a^{2}}{b^{2}}+3 \cdot \frac{a}{b} \cdot \left(-\frac{2 h}{b}\right)$ $\Rightarrow \frac{-8 h^{3}}{b^{3}}=\frac{a}{b}+\frac{a^{2}}{b^{2}}-\frac{6 a h}{b^{2}}$ $\Rightarrow \frac{a}{b}+\frac{a^{2}}{b^{2}}-\frac{6 a h}{b^{2}}+\frac{8 h^{3}}{b^{3}}=0$ or $a^{2} b+a b^{2}+8 h=6 a b h$ or $a b(a+b)+8 h^{2}=6 a b h$ or $\frac{a+b}{h}+\frac{8 h^{2}}{a b}=6$ or $\left| \frac{a+b}{h}+\frac{8 h^{2}}{a b} \right|=6$ © examsnet.com

solution: Solution: Let $L_{1}: y=mx$ (equation of line passes through origin) Intercept made by $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$ are equal $\Rightarrow L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$ are at the same distance from centre of circle $x^{2}+y^{2}-x+3y=0$ Now, centre $\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{-3}{2}\right)$ $\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;$ [∵ centre = (-g - f)] Distance of $L_{1}$ from $\left(\frac{1}{2},-\frac{3}{2}\right)=\frac{\left| m\cdot\frac{1}{2}+\frac{3}{2} \right|}{\sqrt{m^{2}+1}}$ Distance of $L_{2}$ from $\left(\frac{1}{2},-\frac{3}{2}\right)=\frac{\left| \frac{1}{2} - \frac{3}{2} - 1 \right|}{\sqrt{1+1}}$ $\because L_{2}: x+y-1=0$ $\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;$ $[\because y = mx \Rightarrow mx - y = 0]$ $\Rightarrow \frac{\left| \frac{m+3}{2} \right|}{\sqrt{m^{2}+1}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}$ Squaring both sides, we get $\frac{(m+3)^{2}}{4(m^{2}+1)} = \frac{4}{2}$ $\Rightarrow m^{2}+6m+9=8(m^{2}+1)$ $\Rightarrow 7m^{2}-6m-1=0$ $\Rightarrow m=\frac{6 \pm \sqrt{36+28}}{14} = \frac{6 \pm 8}{14}$ $=1, \frac{-1}{7}$ $\therefore L_{1}$ is $y=x$ and $y=\frac{-1}{7}x$ or $x-y=0$ or $x+7y=0$ © examsnet.com

question: $f(x)=\begin{cases} \frac{72^{x}-9^{x}-8^{x}+1}{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{1+\cos x}}, & x \neq 0 \\ k \log 2 \log 3, & x=0 \end{cases}$ Find the value of k for which the function f is continuous.

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: f is continuous at $x=0$ $\therefore \lim\limits_{x \to 0}\; f(x)=f(0)$ $\Rightarrow \lim\limits_{x \to 0} \frac{72^{x}-9^{x}-8^{x}+1}{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{1+\cos x}} = k \log 2 \log 3$ $\Rightarrow k \log 2 \cdot \log 3$ $= \lim\limits_{x \to 0} \frac{(9^{x}-1)(8^{x}-1)(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{1+\cos x})}{2-(1+\cos x)}$ $= \lim\limits_{x \to 0} \left[ \frac{9^{x}-1}{x} \cdot \frac{8^{x}-1}{x} \cdot \frac{x^{2}}{1-\cos x} \cdot (\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{1+\cos x}) \right]$ $= \log 9 \cdot \log 8 \cdot 2 (\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{2})$ $= 2 \log 3 \cdot 3 \log 2 \cdot 4 \sqrt{2}$ $\Rightarrow k \log 3 \cdot \log 2 = 24 \sqrt{2} \log 3 \cdot \log 2$ $\Rightarrow k = 24 \sqrt{2}$ © examsnet.com

question: If $y=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{1+x^{2}}+\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{\sqrt{1+x^{2}}-\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\right)$ , where $x^{2} \le 1$ . Then find $\frac{d y}{d x}$

solution: Solution: $y=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{1+x^{2}}+\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{\sqrt{1+x^{2}}-\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\right)$ Substituting $x^{2}=\cos 2\theta$ $\Rightarrow \theta=\frac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}(x^{2})$ $\therefore y=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{1+\cos 2\theta}+\sqrt{1-\cos 2\theta}}{\sqrt{1+\cos 2\theta}-\sqrt{1-\cos 2\theta}}\right)$ $=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}\cos\theta+\sqrt{2}\sin\theta}{\sqrt{2}\cos\theta-\sqrt{2}\sin\theta}\right)$ $=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1+\tan\theta}{1-\tan\theta}\right)$ $=\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\theta\right)\right)$ $\Rightarrow y=\frac{\pi}{4}+\theta$ $\Rightarrow y=\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}(x^{2})$ $\therefore \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot\left(\frac{-2x}{\sqrt{1-x^{4}}}\right)=\frac{-x}{\sqrt{1-x^{4}}}$ © examsnet.com

solution: Solution: Let $I = \int\limits_{2}^{4} (|x-2|+|x-3|) d x$ $\because x - a = \begin{cases} x - a, & x \ge a \\ -(x - a), & x < a \end{cases}$ $\therefore I = \int\limits_{2}^{4} |x-2| d x + \int\limits_{2}^{3} |x-3| d x + \int\limits_{3}^{4} |x-3| d x$ $= \int\limits_{2}^{4} (x-2) d x - \int\limits_{2}^{3} (x-3) d x + \int\limits_{3}^{4} (x-3) d x$ $= \left( \frac{x^{2}}{2} - 2x \right)_{2}^{4} - \left( \frac{x^{2}}{2} - 3x \right)_{2}^{3} + \left( \frac{x^{2}}{2} - 3x \right)_{3}^{4}$ $= \left[ \left( \frac{16}{2} - 8 \right) - \left( \frac{4}{2} - 4 \right) \right] - \left[ \left( \frac{9}{2} - 9 \right) - \left( \frac{4}{2} - 6 \right) \right] + \left[ \left( \frac{16}{2} - 12 \right) - \left( \frac{9}{2} - 9 \right) \right]$ $= \left| \left[ 0 - (-2) \right] - \left[ \left( \frac{-9}{2} \right) - (-4) \right] + \left[ (-4) - \left( -\frac{9}{2} \right) \right] \right|$ $= \left| 2 + \frac{9}{2} - 4 - 4 + \frac{9}{2} \right| = \left[ 2 + 9 - 8 \right] = 3$ © examsnet.com

question: If a chemical reaction is known to be non-spontaneous at $298\,\text{K}$ but spontaneous at $350\,\text{K}$ . then which among the following conditions is true for the reaction?

options.A: $\Delta G = -$ ve, $\Delta H = -$ ve, $\Delta S = +$ ve
options.B: $\Delta G = +$ ve, $\Delta H = +$ ve, $\Delta S = +\text{v e}$
options.C: $\Delta G = -\text{v e}, \Delta H = +\text{v e}, \Delta S = +\text{v e}$
options.D: $\Delta G = +$ ve, $\Delta H = +$ ve, $\Delta S = -$ ve

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: According to Gibb's free energy, $\Delta G = \Delta H - T \Delta S$ Reaction is non spontancous i.e. $\Delta G > 0$ at $298\,\text{K}$ . As the temperature increases from $298\,\text{K}$ to $350\,\text{K}$ . The reaction becomes spontaneous i.e. $\Delta G < 0$ . $\Delta G = \Delta H - T \Delta S$ $\Delta G < 0$ When $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ are +ve then, $\Delta G$ will be positive till $\Delta H > T \Delta S$ . When the temperature is increased further $\Delta H$ becomes less than $T \Delta S$ i.e. $\Delta H < T \Delta S$ and $\Delta G$ becomes $-\text{v e.}$ Thus, reaction becomes spontancous. © examsnet.com
transcription_status: published educational transcription; original PDF remains authoritative

question: If $\theta \in [0, 2\pi]$ and $\cos 2\theta = \cos \theta + \sin \theta$ then the sum of all values of $\theta$ satisfying the equation is ______

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $\cos 2\theta = \cos \theta + \sin \theta$ $\Rightarrow (\cos^2 \theta - \sin^2 \theta) - (\cos \theta + \sin \theta) = 0$ $\Rightarrow (\cos \theta + \sin \theta)(\cos \theta - \sin \theta - 1) = 0$ $\Rightarrow \cos \theta + \sin \theta = 0$ or $\cos \theta - \sin \theta = 1$ When $\cos \theta + \sin \theta = 0$ , then $\tan \theta = -1$ $\text{then } \theta = n\pi + \frac{3\pi}{4}$ $\Rightarrow \theta = \frac{3\pi}{4}, \frac{7\pi}{4} \in [0, 2\pi]$ and when $\cos \theta - \sin \theta = 1$ , then $\sin \theta + (1 - \cos \theta) = 0$ and $2 \sin \frac{\theta}{2} \left( \cos \frac{\theta}{2} + \sin \frac{\theta}{2} \right) = 0$ and $\sin \frac{\theta}{2} = 0, \cos \frac{\theta}{2} + \sin \frac{\theta}{2} = 0$ $\Rightarrow \frac{\theta}{2} = n\pi, \tan \frac{\theta}{2} = -1$ $\Rightarrow \frac{\theta}{2} = n\pi, \tan \frac{\theta}{2} = -1$ $\Rightarrow \theta = 0, 2\pi \in [0, 2\pi]$ $\theta = \frac{6\pi}{4} \in [0, 2\pi]$ Sum of all values of θ $= \frac{3\pi}{4} + \frac{7\pi}{4} + 0 + 2\pi + \frac{6\pi}{4} = \frac{24\pi}{4}$ © examsnet.com

question: In ΔABC, suppose the radius of the circle opposite to an angle A is denoted by $r_{1}$ , similarly $r_{2} \leftrightarrow$ angle $B, r_{3} \leftrightarrow$ angle C. If $r_{1}=2, r_{2}=3, r_{3}=6$ , what is the value of $r_{1}+r_{2}+r_{3}-r=$ (R - Radius of the circum circle)

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $\because r=\frac{\Delta}{s}, r_{1}=\frac{\Delta}{s-a}, r_{2}=\frac{\Delta}{s-b},$ $r_{3}=\frac{\Delta}{s-c}$ and $2 s=a+b+c$ Then, $r_{1}+r_{2}+r_{3}-r=\frac{\Delta}{s-a}+\frac{\Delta}{s-b}+\frac{\Delta}{s-c}-\frac{\Delta}{s}$ $=\Delta \left( \frac{2s-(a+b)}{(s-a)(s-b)} \right) + \Delta \left( \frac{c}{s(s-c)} \right)$ $=\Delta \frac{2s-2s+c}{(s-a)(s-b)} + \Delta \left( \frac{c}{s(s-c)} \right)$ $=\Delta \left[ \frac{c s(s-c)+c(s-a)(s-b)}{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)} \right]$ $\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;$ $[\because \Delta^{2}=s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)]$ $=\frac{\Delta c}{\Delta^{2}} \left( s(s-c)+(s-a)(s-b) \right)$ $=\frac{c}{\Delta} \left( s^{2} - s c + s^{2} - (a+b)s + a b \right)$ $=\frac{c}{\Delta} \left( 2s^{2} - (a+b+c)s + a b \right)$ $=\frac{c}{\Delta} \left( 2s^{2} - 2s^{2} + a b \right)$ $\;\;\;\;\;$ $[\because 2s = a+b+c]$ $=\frac{a b c}{\Delta} = 4 \left( \frac{a b c}{4 \Delta} \right) = 4R$ © examsnet.com

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Comparing given cquation, $8 x^{2}-24 x y+18 y^{2}-6 x+9 y-5=0$ On comparing with general form $a x^{2}+2 h x y+b y^{2}+2 g x+2 f y+c=0$ $a=8, h=-12, b=18, g=-3, f=\frac{9}{2}, c=-5$ $\because h^{2}=144$ and $a b=8 \times 18=144$ $\Rightarrow h^{2}=a b$ and $a f^{2}=8\left(\frac{9}{2}\right)^{2}=8 \times \frac{81}{4}=2 \times 81=162$ $b g^{2}=18(-3)=18 \times 9=162$ $\Rightarrow a f^{2}=b g^{2}$ $\because h^{2}=a b$ and $a f^{2}=b g^{2}$ ∴ Given pair of lines are parallel. © examsnet.com

question: The angle between the lines represented by $\cos \theta(\cos \theta+1) x^{2}-(2 \cos \theta+\sin^{2} \theta) x y+$ $(1-\cos \theta) y^{2}=0$ is ______

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Given pair of lines, $\cos \theta(\cos \theta+1) x^{2}-(2 \cos \theta+\sin^{2} \theta) x y +(1-\cos \theta) y^{2}=0$ Comparing with $a x^{2}+2 h x y+b y^{2}=0$ $a=\cos \theta(\cos \theta+1)$ $h=-\frac{2 \cos \theta+\sin^{2} \theta}{2}$ $b=1-\cos \theta$ $a+b=\cos^{2} \theta+1$ $h^{2}-ab=\frac{4 \cos^{2} \theta+\sin^{4} \theta+4 \cos \theta \sin^{2} \theta}{4} - \cos \theta (1-\cos^{2} \theta)$ $=\frac{4 \cos^{2} \theta+(1-\cos^{2} \theta)^{2}+4 \cos \theta \sin^{2} \theta-4 \cos \theta \sin^{2} \theta}{4}$ $=\frac{\cos^{4} \theta+2 \cos^{2} \theta+1}{4}=\left(\frac{\cos^{2} \theta+1}{2}\right)^{2}$ If θ be the acute angle between the lines, then $\tan \theta=\frac{2 \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}}{|a+b|}=\frac{2\left(\frac{\cos^{2} \theta+1}{2}\right)}{\cos^{2} \theta+1}=1$ $\Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$ © examsnet.com

question: For the redox reaction $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-} + \mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-} + \mathrm{H}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + \mathrm{CO}_{2} + \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ , the correct coefficients of the reactants for the balanced reaction are respectively $\mathrm{Mn} 0_{4}^{-}, \mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-}$ and $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ ______

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: The unbalanced redox reaction is $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-} + \mathrm{C}, \mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-} + \mathrm{H}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + \mathrm{CO}_{2} + \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ (i) Balanced C atoms $\mathrm{MnO}_{\overset{+7}{4}} + \mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-} + \mathrm{H}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + 2 \mathrm{CO}_{2} + \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ Oxidation state of Mn decreases from $+7$ to $+2$ . To balance the increase or decrease in oxidation number, multiply Mn  containing species with 2 and C containing species with $5.$ $2 \mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-} + 5 \mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + 10 \mathrm{CO}_{2}$ (ii) Balance $\text{'O'}$ atoms by adding 8 water molecules to the product side. $2 \mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-} + 5 \mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + 10 \mathrm{CO}_{2} + 8 \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ (iii) Balance 'H' atoms by adding $16 \mathrm{H}^{+}$ ions to the reactant side. $2 \mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-} + 5 \mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-} + 16 \mathrm{H}^{+} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + 10 \mathrm{CO}_{2} + 8 \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ Hence, $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-} \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-} \Rightarrow 5, \mathrm{H}^{+}=16$ © examsnet.com

question: When the temperature of 2 moles of an ideal gas is increased by $20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ at constant pressure. find the work involved in the process.

solution: Solution: Temperature of an ideal gas increased by $=20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ i.e. $T_{2}$ Initial temperature of gas, $T_{1}=0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ Number of moles, $n=2$ Formula of work done, $W=-nR(T_{2}-T_{1})$ $W=-2 R(20-0)$ $W=-40 R$ But work involved in the process, $W=+ve$ $W=40 R$ Here, $R=$ Rate constant i.e. $8.314\,\mathrm{JK}^{-1}\,\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ $W=40 \times 8.314=332.56\,\mathrm{JK}^{-1}\,\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ © examsnet.com

question: Using the data provided, find the value of equilibrium constant for the following reaction at $298\ \text{K}$ and 1 atm pressure. $\mathrm{NO}_{(g)} + \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NO}_{2}(g)$ $\Delta_{f} H^{0}(\mathrm{NO}_{(g)}) = 90.4\ \text{kJ}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ $\Delta_{f} H^{0}(\mathrm{NO}_{2(g)}) = 32.48\ \text{kJ}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ $\Delta S^{0} \text{@} 298\ \text{K} = -70.8\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$ $\operatorname{antilog}(0.50) = 3162$

solution: Solution: $\mathrm{NO}(g) + \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_{2}(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NO}_{2}(g)$ Given, $\Delta_{f} H^{0}(\mathrm{NO}_{(g)}) = 90.4\ \text{kJ}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ $\Delta H^{\circ} = \Sigma \Delta H^{\circ}$ product $-\Sigma \Delta_{f} H^{\circ}(\mathrm{NO})$ $= 3248 - 90.4$ $= -57.92\ \text{kJ}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ We know that. Standard Gibb's free energy, $\Delta G^{\circ} = \Delta H^{\circ} - T \Delta S^{\circ}$ $= -57.92 - 298 \times (-70.8)$ $= -57.92 + 21.098 = -36.82\ \text{kJ/mol}$ $= -38.82 \times 10^{3}\ \text{J/mol}$ We also know, $\Delta G^{\circ} = -2.303 RT \log K_{eq}$ Here, $K_{eq} =$ Equilibrium constant $-36.82 \times 10^{3} = -2303 \times 8.314 \times 298 \times \log K_{eq}$ $\log K_{eq} = \frac{36.82}{5.70584}$ $\log K_{eq} = 0.501$ $K_{eq} = \operatorname{antilog} 0.501$ $= 3162 \times 10^{6}$ © examsnet.com

question: Calculate the pOH of $0.10 \; \mathrm{M}  \mathrm{HCl}$ solution.
